frontier.hypothesis: Target's preheader copy is emitted by loop.c into an already-formed preheader rather than surviving from source, which is why it is use-once and why no combine escape explains it.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c is the largest emit_move_insn producer in the s28 census (14 sites) and is the only producer in that census closed by SCORE alone and never by a dump. Its preheader emissions (loop-invariant hoists and giv/biv initializations) land exactly where target's addu a3,a0,zero sits - after the blez, before the links load - and run BEFORE combine, so a copy loop.c creates would still have to survive combine; but a copy loop.c creates for a value whose use is inside the loop body would not have the single in-block LOG_LINK that kills ours.
frontier.next_probe: On the join chassis (candidate_alt_join_shape_6.c, already applied-and-dumped once this session), read tmp/grind/func_80017848/dumps/ings.loop for func_80017848 and locate every insn loop.c ADDED to either preheader; compare against ings.cse2. Then build cells that give the base pointer a loop-carried shape loop.c would hoist or strength-reduce (e.g. the record pointer advanced by the loop instead of indexed by i), and check ings.loop for an emitted preheader move. This is the first producer probe run on a chassis whose preheader is block-for-block target's.

frontier.hypothesis: Escape #1 (a second use of the copy destination downstream of the base add) is cheaper on the join chassis than on the BASE chassis, because cse's make_regs_eqv promotion already makes the base add read the copy destination, so a second use no longer has to fight a fold.
frontier.mechanism: s31 priced escape-1 sites on the BASE chassis at 6 (in-body), 9 (bottom test), 12 (pre-join) and 19-22 (post-loop), and s31's cell P failed specifically because cse re-folded sh2 + (s32)q back onto the available base pseudo before combine ran. On the join chassis the promotion goes the other way - the base add reads q, not p - so a bottom-test or in-body use of q is no longer a redundant recomputation of an available expression and may survive to combine as a genuine second reference.
frontier.next_probe: On the P1 and P4 bodies, sweep second-use sites for q that replace an instruction target already spends: (a) the do-while bottom test written through q, (b) the in-body base+i address written through q, (c) loop 2's guard pointer read replaced by q where the value is provably live. Score each and, for every cell reaching 127 build insns, run tmp/grind/func_80017848/s34/dis.sh and check whether the residual is instruction-level or seat-level.

frontier.hypothesis: combine.c:902 (succ && !all_adjacent && reg_used_between_p (dest, succ, i3)) is still unspelled, and reaching it needs a second in-block feeder for the base add that cse cannot equate with the guard's shift.
frontier.mechanism: The refusal fires only on a three-insn combination, i.e. when the base add carries two LOG_LINKS. R1's (slot_a << 5) << 1 failed because combine's shift simplification re-merges it before try_combine looks at the add. A feeder that is not an arithmetic identity of the guard's shift - derived from t2, from a subtraction, or from a differently-typed intermediate - would survive to combine and create the second link.
frontier.next_probe: On body_P1.c, build cells whose loop-2 preheader recomputes the base's shift operand through an expression cse cannot equate with sh2 (e.g. via the guard's t2 value, or a subtraction of two already-live quantities), then read tmp/grind/func_80017848/dumps/ings.combine for whether try_combine reports a three-insn attempt at the base add. If no attempt is made even with two in-block LOG_LINKS present, record combine.c:902 as measured-unreachable for this CFG with the dump as the predicate evidence.
